title: Fix the history check failure and gate it in the verified-landing path
summary: Commit 64ecdc9 carries an Athena-Job trailer for one job but adds another job's closing records, so the invariant's landing check rejects it in `athena check --history`. The reading is: find why the landing path built that commit, fix it, and make the full-history check part of what a landing must pass, so a gate change cannot land as verified while it fails.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests, plus Markdown docs.
Regression tests for the mismatch and for the landing-time history gate; cargo test and clippy must pass.
The 'cannot land as verified while the history check fails' rule is enforced in code, not prose.
The root cause is cited from the code path and the failing message; enforcement.md lists refusal and allowing tests.
One focused fix: the root cause plus the landing-time history gate.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier can run, including `cargo run -- check --history`.
I recovered the failing rule from invariant.rs:255-265 and the CI history job instead of asking.

assumptions: History cannot be rewritten (the repository's rules say published history is never rewritten), so commit 64ecdc9 stays. The fix must make the history check pass on the current tip some other way.

The in-process gate on the landing commit (run.rs land_or_block / build_commit) did not catch the mismatch that invariant.rs:255-265 flags in the history check. The producer must find out why, for example by trailers and records drawn from different jobs, or by a gate path that skips the landing rule.

The fix for 'a gate change can't land as verified while the full-history check fails' is a mechanism, not prose. Candidates are an in-process history check on the candidate's tree at landing, or a check entry run before landing. The producer chooses and records the call.
The tests live beside the code: the crates/athena-gate unit tests, and the CLI integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests if the behavior reaches the CLI.
question: Should the exemption of 64ecdc9 be recorded in [history].exempt in athena.toml? I assume not, because that list is for commits that predate Athena. I assume the fix is to the gate and its tests, plus a way to accept this one commit that the producer must pick and justify.

acceptance_criteria.text: The root cause of the mismatch between the Athena-Job trailer and the closing records in commit 64ecdc9 is identified in the change description, and the code path that produced it is fixed.

Run `cargo test --locked`. A new regression test reproduces a landing whose Athena-Job trailer names a different job from the closing records it adds, and shows the in-process gate refuses it or the landing path can no longer produce it.
Run `cargo run --locked -- check --history` from the repository root. It reports no violation for 64ecdc9 and exits 0. Any exemption or handling of that commit is explained in a code or doc comment.

Run `cargo test --locked`. A new test shows that a change to the gate (crates/athena-gate) which makes the full-history check fail cannot reach a verified landing, because the landing path runs the history check on the resulting tree or tip and refuses.

docs/enforcement.md (and CHANGELOG.md if it records behavior changes) name the new mechanism with its refusal and allowing tests. Any change to athena.toml is listed as a deliverable and named in a criterion.
Run `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`. Both are clean, and `cargo test --locked` passes.

out_of_scope: Changing CI workflows, setup.sh, or toolchain, lint, and rustfmt configuration.
Redesigning the trailer format or the job-identification rule beyond what the fix needs.
departures: Higher cost, longer time, and lower pass odds than the reference. The root cause is not yet known, the fix touches the gate and the landing path, and the verifier cannot reproduce the real history failure without a regression test that stands in for it.
